memo.verdict: Bearish on Repsol (REP-ES) at EUR 29.18 (2026-10-05); park. Conviction medium: a Triaging-stage view resting on consensus earnings and the stock's own multiple history, not on a Viewforth model. The record takes the other side of the market's thesis: a cyclical-peak case dressed as a cash-return case, not compelling at EUR 29.18. The park is on the return and the riskiness, not the gate: no D or F sits on management ('No mediocre management' B), business quality ('Business' C), predictability ('Transmission' B) or trackability ('Leading indicators' A), so the gate does not fire. The case re-opens on price (below about EUR 19 on the modal path; below about EUR 22 at the conceded 7.80x anchor) or on evidence that the European refining margin has structurally re-based (the Spanish refining margin indicator above USD 15 a barrel through Q4 2027 with the company's realised premium above USD 8). The record names the shares as the price-moved-against-the-park pattern with the park on the sell side.
case: The change is external, extreme and at its peak. Middle East and Russian supply disruption (0.8 to 0.9 million barrels a day lost through Hormuz; up to 1.0 million barrels a day of Russian middle distillates) lifted the Spanish refining margin indicator from USD 5.60 a barrel in H1 2025 to USD 12.40 in H1 2026 and a record USD 38 in Q3 2026, about five standard deviations above the USD 6.50 mid-cycle the company plans on. Dated Brent averaged USD 92.30 in H1 2026 and spiked to USD 144 before de-escalating once. The structural part is smaller but real: 35 European refineries closed since 2009, 20 percent of regional capacity; Morgan Stanley expects mid-cycle margins 30 percent above history. That is the only durable external tailwind; the slower external forces (European diesel demand down 4.7 percent in June 2026, electrification, EU carbon at about EUR 77 a tonne, the methane regulation, Asian refining capacity after 2027, Chinese chemical capacity, US exports to Europe up 17 percent sequentially) are headwinds. The company's own cycle is at a peak: EBITDA fell from EUR 13,575 million in 2022 to EUR 6,660 million in 2025 (Redburn's basis) and the 2022 peak was followed by a halving of Viewforth-definition EPS (EUR 3.35 to EUR 2.20). 'External forces' C; 'Revenue and demand cycle' D; 'Supply side' B (feedstock flexibility worth a USD 10.00 premium in Q2 2026; the cost EUR 2.4 billion of inventory).

The internal change is genuine, incremental and already in the numbers. Three of the screen's forces are strong and dated: perimeter reduction A (18 to 10 upstream countries; UK assets into Neo Next+ at 24 percent; 25 percent of upstream sold to EIG at USD 19 billion in 2022; eight rotations including Masdar's 49.99 percent of 705 MW at EUR 849 million enterprise value); shareholder returns A (share capital reduced 9 percent between 2024 and 2025; the second 2026 buyback raised to EUR 500 million); strategy change B (the 2026 to 2028 plan with 55 percent of capex to Iberia and 34 percent to the United States); guidance raised B (distributions, not an operating target; formal cash-flow guidance suspended in Q1 2026). The red-flag check passes on every count. But there is no chief executive change (D; in post since 2014), the strategy is "written in stone", price rises are absent (D; EUR 50 million of extra fuel discounts in Q2 2026), and the internal change on its own is worth perhaps EUR 0.5 to 0.8 of mid-cycle earnings per share. 'Internal forces' B; 'Change Forces' C.

'Financial Outputs' have improved enormously and are forecast to give half of it back. Adjusted net income EUR 2,711 million in H1 2026 against EUR 1,155 million; FY2026 consensus EPS up 133 percent in twelve months; revenue +35.5 percent in Q2 2026; EBITDA margin 16.0 percent against 7.5 percent; gearing 11.3 percent from 14.0 percent; net debt including leases 1.02x trailing EBITDA from 2.40x. Upgrades to FY2026 and FY2027 over the next six months are probable ('Sell-side upgrades' B): Q3 spot margins of USD 34 to 38 sit far above the USD 20 Redburn used and the USD 20 full-year level the chief executive guided; Jefferies says Q3 refining cash flow alone exceeds the whole 2026 buyback announced so far; the revision skew is overwhelmingly upward (FY2026 mean EPS +42.7 percent over three months; A). The record's own FY2026 estimate is about EUR 5.6 against the EUR 5.40 median. But the same consensus has EPS EUR 5.40 to 4.05 to 3.59 (−25.0 percent then −11 percent), EBITDA down 31 percent FY2026 to FY2028, revenue −13.1 percent in FY2027, the brokers'-basis EBITDA margin 16.4 percent to 13.0 percent, and upgrades to FY2028 are less likely (mean up 4.6 percent over one month, down 0.3 percent over twelve). The inference from the dashboard: estimates chase the margin, targets chase the price (mean target EUR 29.90 against EUR 29.53), ratings are cut as targets are hit (buy share down 13 points to 31 percent); the late-cycle shape of an upgrade cycle. 'Goldilocks growth' D: growth far above 40 percent over six months (the over-extrapolation category; H2 2026 EPS about EUR 2.90 against EUR 1.17 in H2 2025), then negative over eighteen months (F) and three years (F); from the FY2025 base of EUR 2.32 to FY2028's EUR 3.59 is +15.7 percent a year, inside the band but delivered entirely in 2026 and partly given back. 'Staircase' C: near steps B (the October tranche, Q3 results 29-Oct-26, the January dividend, Pikka at 80,000 barrels a day gross plateau), mid steps C (2027 buybacks, Venezuela doubling from 71,000 boe/d, two rotations, a possible upstream listing against Cartagena and Tarragona turnarounds and the Spanish election), far steps D (Morgan Stanley's "material reduction in buybacks" in 2028). 'Financial Outputs' C.
counter_case: The strongest case against, in its strongest form. European refining scarcity is structural, not cyclical: 20 percent of the region's capacity has closed since 2009, the Middle East and Russian disruptions have persisted for a year and may persist for two more, Europe cannot build refineries, and Morgan Stanley's own mid-cycle is 30 percent above history. Repsol is the most levered major to that scarcity, with a complexity premium of USD 10 a barrel that is skill, not luck. On a margin of USD 15, earnings per share stay above EUR 5 (the bull brokers' FY2027 at EUR 6.2 to 6.5 and FY2028 at EUR 4.7 to 6.0), the company reaches net cash in 2027 and buys back 6 to 7 percent of itself a year, the dividend grows 6 percent, and a multiple held at 7.5x on EUR 5 of earnings is EUR 37.50 plus EUR 3.65 of dividends in three years, a 12 percent a year return before the share count does its work: with 6 percent a year of buybacks reflected in per-share earnings, EUR 5.00 becomes about EUR 5.60 by 2031 and the three-year return reaches about 17 percent a year, close to the bar. The 2026 free cash flow yield is 27 percent; net cash arrives in 2027; 6 to 7 percent a year of buybacks on an 8x multiple compounds to 20 percent without any re-rating. The evidence for it: the Q3 margin at USD 38 after a year of forecasts of normalisation; Jefferies, Goldman, RBC and Barclays at EUR 34 to 38; sector-leading estimate momentum; Technical Momentum A; the balance sheet. At Building Block level the bull adds: the 'Foundations' are better than C because the complexity premium is structural, Spain's demand is uniquely resilient and the balance sheet is TotalEnergies-grade; the case is a 'Major Corporate Change' at B with capital discipline and distributions as the change and the 2026 upgrades as the output; the 'Investment Case' is simple and robust because the balance sheet is near net cash, the dividend is covered five times, and the downside is a lower buyback, not a cut.

What the record concedes. The near-term upgrades to FY2026 and FY2027 are probable, and H2 2026 earnings may beat the consensus of about EUR 2.90 a share. The dividend is secure at any margin in the range discussed. The complexity premium is real and repeatable. The structural closure argument raises the floor of the mid-cycle above USD 6.50, which is why the record concedes the 7.80x anchor and shows the return at it. The balance sheet means the downside is a lower buyback, not distress. The 2026 cash, the balance sheet, the inputs to the 'Major Corporate Change' pattern, and all three 'Foundations' facts are conceded.
triggers: - The case re-opens on price: below about EUR 19 on the modal path (the bar-clearing price EUR 18.6 at eighteen months, EUR 15.7 at three years); below about EUR 22 at the conceded 7.80x anchor (EUR 22.1 and EUR 18.4); about EUR 17.0 at eighteen months under the drop-through case.

- The case re-opens on evidence of a structural re-basing: the Spanish refining margin indicator above USD 15 a barrel through Q4 2027 with the realised premium above USD 8; the record would then re-anchor its mid-cycle.

- Invalidate levels for the record's bearish case: spreads above USD 15 a barrel for the full year 2028; a 2028 buyback guided at or above EUR 1.5 billion with net cash; a sustained 7.8x on FY2028 earnings above EUR 4.50; a windfall levy enacted at 1.2 percent of domestic revenue (the levy moves the entry price down about EUR 1.50, not the direction).

- Alarm levels: spreads above USD 15 through Q4 2027; cumulative 2026 to 2027 buybacks above EUR 3.5 billion at gearing below 15 percent; the five-year multiple series printing above 8.20x (a new high); a dated Middle East ceasefire or Hormuz reopening; a PSOE-led coalition with a majority for budget measures; the 24-month-forward multiple below 6.80x (the five-year 90th percentile) as the first sign of the de-rating.
- The bull case's own refutation level: crack spreads below USD 8.00 for two consecutive quarters with 2027 buybacks guided below EUR 1.0 billion.
- The first sign of the growth engine slowing: the Q4 2026 margin indicator against the USD 38 Q3 print; a cut beyond consensus would show first in the Q4 2026 or Q1 2027 indicator.
